name: Honasa Consumer Ltd
title: Honasa Consumer Ltd - 544014 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 net sales up 36% with EBITDA margin 12.7% and gross margin ~70%, driven by volume; management kept the 150-200 bps FY27 margin frame but called it "conservative" and said Q3 margin should hold near 12.5%.

triggers.label: Q2 net sales growth 36%
triggers.quote: Honasa has grown the net sales at 36%, while doubling our EBITDA and holding a solid 12.7% EBITDA profile.

triggers.label: Price increases offsetting crude costs
triggers.quote: we have been able to manage our gross margin profile at 70% by right kind of cost management as well as price increase measures that we have taken.

triggers.label: Stock pressure down in Mamaearth stores
triggers.quote: The Nielsen-measured inventory turns have also improved, so stock pressure has actually gone down further.

guidance.quote: from our next four years perspective, we want to get to a 15% EBITDA margin profile.
We are confident of being able to hold our current trajectory and be in the same range of around 12.5.

prior_guidance_check.quote: Mamaearth continues its high teens growth trajectory in Q2 as well.
from our next four years perspective, we want to get to a 15% EBITDA margin profile.

red_flags.label: Management declined to give FY27 margin-year numbers; said 'We necessarily don't have a year-wise goal'
red_flags.quote: We necessarily don't have a year-wise goal.

red_flags.label: Volume growth below value growth; price-driven growth from crude-linked hikes
red_flags.quote: There is price-driven growth, which is also built in hair, especially on account of the crude impact that we have seen.

I wouldn't be able to comment on percentages.

summary.headline: Honasa Q2 FY27 net sales grew 36% YoY with EBITDA roughly doubled to a 12.7% margin; management guides to around 12.5% for the coming quarters.
summary.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 the highest-growth quarter since the IPO, with net sales up 36% YoY, EBITDA roughly doubled at a 12.7% margin, and gross margin held at about 70% despite crude-linked cost pressure. Growth was mostly volume-led (UVG 31.3%), with price increases also contributing. Focus categories now make up 80%+ of revenue and grew more than 40%, and younger brands grew 45%+ (40%+ excluding The Derma Co.). Management reiterated a 15% EBITDA margin ambition over four years but declined to set year-wise targets.

financial_highlights.change: Highest growth quarter since listing (12 quarters)
Held despite crude cost pressure, aided by price increases

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin delta from A&P and mix efficiencies

financial_highlights.change: Focus categories now 80%+ of revenue, up from about 70% earlier
Consistent in Q2, both online and offline

segments.name: Mamaearth
segments.commentary: Growing at a high-teens rate in Q2, with e-commerce and offline both growing high teens. Available at about 3.2 lakh outlets, with about 26% YoY ND growth and 40%+ modern trade offtake growth.

segments.name: The Derma Co.
segments.commentary: Second INR1,000 crore+ brand, with ARR continuing in the INR1,000 crore+ range. Management said it continues strong profitable growth and launched body wash.

segments.name: Younger brands (Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's, BBlunt, Staze, Reginald Men)
segments.commentary: Grew 45%+ YoY, and 40%+ excluding The Derma Co. and Reginald. BBlunt hair colour grew 100%+ YoY after its relaunch last year.

segments.name: Focus categories
segments.commentary: Contribute 80%+ of revenue and grew more than 40%. Management puts the addressable focus-category market at about INR50,000 crore, with the company at about 5% share.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce grew 20%+, general trade and modern trade each grew about 40%. Offline same-store growth was about 30%+. Management said the mix shift is toward more profitable channels such as offline and quick commerce.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of a 15% EBITDA margin over the next four years, with no year-wise goal set; some years may prioritise growth with only 50-70 bps of margin expansion.
Management is confident of holding the current trajectory and staying around 12.5% EBITDA margin in the near term, after the 13.5% H1 level that analysts noted included one-offs.
Management will track YoY growth rather than sequential growth. Q3 will be sequentially higher than Q2 due to seasonality, but no percentage was given.

Management said it sees no benefit to being too aggressive and prefers to be conservative on the 150-200 bps annual margin improvement guidance, while describing the current level as a foundation it is comfortable maintaining.
Management said it is considering a hair colour entry from another brand in the portfolio and will announce it at launch.
capex_capacity: Offline distribution: Mamaearth at about 3.2 lakh outlets; The Derma Co. at 65,000 outlets; Mamaearth outlet reach is about 300,000 in a different count. Nielsen-measured face wash share for The Derma Co. is about 1.2%.
Management said 80% of growth delta is coming from existing stores and distribution, with distribution expansion as a secondary driver.
Launched or relaunched products include the Mamaearth Chaayos tinted lip balm collaboration, The Derma Co. body wash, Aqualogica tinted sun serum and mist, and BBlunt curl care.
Opened schools for preschoolers as part of community initiatives. No capex or capacity figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Volume growth (31.3%) exceeded value growth in Q2; management attributed the gap to MRP/price increases taken due to crude costs, plus channel and brand mix.
Management expects no significant overall mix shift toward offline, with e-commerce and offline both growing strongly through different brand portfolios.

Market share gains: 140 bps in face wash and 50 bps in shampoo (Nielsen core categories). Face wash is the largest category, followed by sunscreen, and face wash was the fastest-growing category, followed by shampoo, sunscreen and moisturizers, which each grew 20%+.
Management highlighted hair colour as a category transitioning from dye to creme format, with overall hair colour penetration in India low versus 5%+ globally.
Per capita beauty spend in India is among the lowest in Asia, per management, with Indonesia at about 4x India's per capita spend.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth for younger brands excluding The Derma Co., given e-commerce growth of only about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said younger brands excluding The Derma Co. grew 40%+. Some D2C sales sit outside the e-commerce channel figures reported.

qa_highlights.question: What supports Mamaearth holding high-teens or mid-teens growth in H2 against a higher base?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is coming equally from online and offline, with e-commerce also growing in the high teens. Management said 80% of the growth delta comes from existing stores, and SAH has grown faster than market share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume growth lag value growth this quarter, and will the mix shift to offline reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap was due to price increases from crude-linked costs and channel and brand mix. Management does not expect a significant overall mix change toward offline.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins evolve, given younger brands need higher A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: The 15% EBITDA target over four years already assumes younger brand growth and new launches. Management has no year-wise margin goal and some years may show only 50-70 bps of expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 150-200 bps margin guidance be raised given Q2 strength?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers being conservative, but the current level is a foundation it is comfortable maintaining. Near-term EBITDA is expected to hold around 12.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the brand and margin plan for Aqualogica and Dr. Sheth's?
qa_highlights.answer: Aqualogica is expanding into body care and moisturizers and gaining Gen Z acceptance. Dr. Sheth's is being repositioned for active consumers, with higher-age offerings such as Botox and collagen.

risks_watch: Crude-linked input cost pressure, which management has offset with price increases. Gross margin held at about 70%, but further inflation could pressure margins.
Higher A&P needs for younger brands and festive and activation spend in Q3 and Q4 may limit margin expansion versus the 12.5% near-term view.
Growth may slow against a higher H2 base, especially for Mamaearth (high-teens) and younger brands.
Volume growth trailing value growth may persist if price increases continue to contribute.
Limited disclosure on brand-level growth, with a new hair colour brand entry under consideration and an unspecified timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, quality of growth and market share. Management was cautious on margin trajectory, avoiding year-wise targets and declining to raise guidance. It also avoided some detailed questions, such as brand-level growth excluding The Derma Co.
key_quotes: Honasa has grown the net sales at 36%, while doubling our EBITDA and holding a solid 12.7% EBITDA profile.
Conservative probably the better place to be.
80% of the growth delta is from current stores, and which is what gives us even more confidence that this will continue next year as well.
As we have communicated, from our next four years perspective, we want to get to a 15% EBITDA margin profile.

growth.why: Q2 net sales +36% YoY with EBITDA roughly doubled at 12.7% margin; management guides to holding around 12.5% EBITDA margin and a 15% margin ambition over four years, but gives no revenue growth guidance and no capacity additions, with growth attributed to existing stores, distribution, volume and pricing rather than specific capacity or orders.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides to holding about 12.5% EBITDA margin after 12.7% in Q2 and 13.5% in H1 (which included one-offs), and a 15% ambition over four years with no year-wise target; some years may add only 50-70 bps, and festive A&P in Q3-Q4 may cap expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity additions or capex figures were disclosed; management said 80% of growth delta comes from existing stores and distribution, with distribution expansion secondary.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 UVG was 31.3%, Mamaearth is growing high-teens with online and offline both up, focus categories grew 40%+ and younger brands 45%+, though growth may slow against a higher H2 base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given, so no capacity announcement can be inferred.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to raise guidance, said it prefers to be conservative on the 150-200 bps annual margin improvement, and framed 12.5% as a level to hold rather than a base to beat.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Crude-linked input cost pressure, higher A&P for younger brands and festive spend in Q3-Q4 could push margin below the 12.5% near-term view, though gross margin held at about 70%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is considering a hair colour entry from another brand in the portfolio, to be announced at launch, and recently launched body wash, tinted sun serum and BBlunt curl care; BBlunt hair colour grew 100%+ after relaunch.

rows.label: Offline and quick-commerce channel mix shift
rows.why: General trade and modern trade each grew about 40% and offline same-store growth was 30%+, but management does not expect a significant overall mix shift toward offline.

rows.label: Price increases offsetting crude costs
rows.why: Price increases taken for crude costs drove part of the gap between 31.3% volume growth and lower value growth, and gross margin held at about 70%.

rows.label: Focus category share gains
rows.why: Focus categories are 80%+ of revenue and grew 40%+ against a roughly INR50,000 crore addressable market where the company holds about 5% share; face wash share rose 140 bps.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, market share and the quality of growth, but cautious on margins by avoiding year-wise targets and declining to raise guidance; analysts pressed on younger brands excluding The Derma Co., the offline mix shift and the sustainability of margins.
